question: You are developing a retail application on Vertex Al that uses a large language model to give customers real - time product recommendations. The app uses text, code, images, audio, and video prompts to communicate with customers. You need to minimize the app lication's latency to ensure a responsive and delightful user experience. What should you do?

options.A: Avoid using system instructions to prevent overly long responses.
options.B: Enable streaming responses from the model to process the output in real time.
options.D: Avoid using the max_output_tokens parameter to prevent overly long responses.

question: Your company is running Al/ML workloads on graphics processing units(GPUs) within Google Kubernetes Engine(GKE). These workloads are deployed across production and development projects, with the production environment being business critical and operating 24/7. You need to ensure that the GPU capacity is always available during scaling events, without being limited by overall GPU availability. You also need the ability to shift unused GPU capacity from production to development projects as needed. You want to follow Google - recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.A: Create an owner project with shared reservations, and then configure the production project and development project as consumer projects to consume capacity.
options.B: Create a reservation in the production project, and then transfer the reservation to the development project when needed.
options.C: Create a shared reservation in the production project, and then add the development project as a consumer project to move capacity when needed.
options.D: Create a reservation in the production project, and then create a separate reservation in the development project to secure capacity.

question: You are setting up a new regional environment for your business needs. You plan to migrate more than 2 TB of data from the us - centra11 region to the asia - southeast1 region. The transfer should occur as quickly as possible. If the transfer is interrupted, t he operation must resume where it left off and copy only new or modified objects. What should you do?

options.A: Leverage Cloud Composer to orchestrate a data pipeline that copies objects from the source bucket to the destination bucket.
options.B: Utilize Storage Transfer Service(STS) to migrate objects to the destination bucket in the target region. Once the transfer is complete, delete the original source bucket objects.
options.C: Use the goloud storage op command to copy the objects. Be careful to manage potential naming conflicts to ensure data integrity.
options.D: Uswestiour storage rsync - recursive command to replicate the source bucket to a new target bucket in the us - west1 region.

question: You are responsible for the architecture of a critical ecommerce application. The application's web frontends run on Compute Engine instances deployed across multiple zones within a single region. The architecture must be highly available and self - healing. If a zone becomes unavailable, the system must automatically recreate the lost capacity in the available zones. To maximize efficiency, you need to ensure that all provisioned compute resources actively serve traffic during normal operations, and user tra ffic is automatically and seamlessly directed away from any failed instance or zone. What should you do?

options.A: Create three separate zonal managed instance groups(MIGs), and use Cloud DNS with weighted routing to distribute traffic across the public IP address of an instance in each MIG.
options.B: Configure a regional external Application Load Balancer with a primary regional managed instance group(MIG) as its backend service, and configure a second regional MIG as a failover backend.
options.C: Create a single regional managed instance group(MIG) configured to span all three zones. Place a regional external Application Load Balancer in front of the MIG, and configure its backend service with a health check.
options.D: Create a single regional unmanaged instance group spanning all three zones. Place a regional external Application Load Balancer in front of the group, and configure its backend service with a health check.

question: You are designing the architecture for a stateless, public - facing, containerized web application. The marketing department uses this web application to run unpredictable flash sales that cause sudden, massive spikes in user traffic. The application is a cr itical revenue driver and must always be available and responsive to users. Your design must automatically handle high traffic fluctuations and allow for new application versions to be deployed with zero downtime and a safe, fast rollback capability. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application to a regional Managed Instance Group(MIG). Configure a CPU - based autoscaling policy and use the MIG's rolling update feature for deployments.
options.B: Deploy the application to a Google Kubernetes Engine(GKE) cluster. Use the Recreate deployment strategy to roll out new application versions.
options.C: Deploy the application as a Cloud Run service. Configure request - based auto - scaling and use gradual rollouts by splitting traffic between revisions.
options.D: Deploy the application to a single, large Compute Engine instance and use a startup script to pull and run the latest container image on boot.

question: You are migrating a large, on - premises application to Google Cloud. The application consists of several interconnected virtual machines. You want to create a detailed migration plan to ensure a smooth migration with minimal effort. You need to understand t he existing environment, identify dependencies, and estimate the total cost of ownership(TCO) in the cloud. What should you do?

options.A: Use Config Connector to declare the desired state of your Google Cloud resources in Kubernetes - style manifests.
options.B: Use the Google Cloud Migration Center to perform an automated discovery and assessment of the on - premises environment.
options.C: Write a custom script to query the Sphere API for virtual machine information and then import it into BigQuery for analysis.
options.D: Use the Google Cloud pricing calculator to input the specifications of your on - premises servers and receive a TCO estimate.

question: You are migrating a critical, on - premises, three - tier ecommerce application to Google Cloud. The application has tightly coupled dependencies between its web, application, and database tiers. The business has strict performance and availability requirement s and is concerned about the risks associated with an"all - at - once" migration. You want to follow Google - recommended practices to create a migration plan that systematically addresses application dependencies and validates post - migration performance before the final production cutover. What should you do?

options.A: Redesign the application to be cloud - native using microservices before migration to eliminate dependencies and simplify workload testing.
options.B: Use dependency mapping to group application components into waves, create a phased migration plan, and incorporate pertormance testing for each wave.
options.C: Plan a'lift and shift" migration for all application tiers to be executed simultaneously over a single weekend to minimize downtime.
options.D: Prioritize the establishment of a high - bandwidth, low - latency Cloud Interconnect connection, and then plan to migrate the database servers first.

question: You are designing the access control strategy for a new system that will store highly sensitive financial reports in a series of Cloud Storage buckets. Each bucket holds a specific type of sensitive data. Your company uses Google Workspace, and all employee roles are managed through Google Groups. The design must allow members of these groups to access only the reports they are authorized to see. The company's governance policy has two additional, critical requirements: All access must be directly tied to an employee's corporate identity for clear audit trails. The access model must be simple to operate and scalable. What should you do?

options.A: Generate and distribute time-limited signed URLs to grant users temporary, per-object access.
options.B: Maintain fine-grained access control, and use default object ACLs to grant the required permissions to the Google Groups.
options.C: Grant the IAM role roles/storage.objectAdmin to all authorized Google Groups to simplify permission management.
options.D: Enable uniform bucket-level access on the buckets, and grant predefined storage IAM roles to the Google Groups.

question: A large enterprise is building a file processing pipeline on Google Cloud. The pipeline ingests the raw files, which are then accessed by a fleet of hundreds of Compute Engine virtual machines(VMs) in a single region for parallel processing. These VMs need concurrent, low - latency read and write access to a shared file system. You need to implement a storage solution that delivers the highest possible throughput to minimize the overall processing time. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Filestore Zonal instance in each zone where the VMs are running. Mount the Filestore file share on each Compute Engine VM.
options.B: Create a Filestore enterprise instance in the same region as the VMS. Mount the rilestore tile share on each Compute Engine VM.
options.C: Use a multi - region Cloud Storage bucket to store the files.
options.D: Create a Regional Persistent Disk and attach it to all VMs in multi - writer mode.

question: You are leading a large - scale Google Cloud implementation project. Your development teams need to deploy applications, but they lack deep expertise in cloud - native patterns. This leads to inconsistent and insecure deployments, such as GKE clusters without proper logging and overly permissive IAM roles. You need to implement a system that empowers these teams to deploy complete, pre - approved architectural patterns in a self - service manner. The system must ensure security and consistency by default while main taining high developer velocity and avoiding manual approval bottlenecks. What should you do?

options.A: Enforce a mandatory CI/CD pipeline using Cloud Build that requires every Terraform deployment to be reviewed and approved before the Terraform apply step can run.
options.B: Create a central Cloud Monitoring dashboard and a set of custom alerts that fire whenever a non - compliant resource is detected.
options.C: Use a combination of organization policies to restrict resource configurations and IAM recommender to periodically suggest improvements.
options.D: Use Servie Catalog to define, govern, and offer a portfolio of approved products. Include Terraform scripts into Service Catalog items.

question: You created a Cloud Monitoring dashboard for your dev environment to view real - time application metrics. The Ops team wants a similar dashboard to monitor the production environment. You want to minimize time and effort as you assist the Ops team with thei r dashboard request. What should you do?

options.A: Create a shared document and list every step you performed to create the dashboard. The Ops team can use the document to build their own dashboard.
options.B: Share your dashboard and send the shared dashboard URL to the Ops team.
options.C: Export your dashboard to a JSON file and share it with the Ops team.
options.D: Grant viewer permission to the Ops team in your project so they can recreate the charts in their dashboard from the console

question: You are designing the observability strategy for a new microservices application running on Google Kubernetes Engine(GKE). The application consists of multiple services(e.g.frontend , orders, payments). During load testing, you observe an error in the frontend service's logs, but you cannot find the corresponding logs in the downstream services to investigate the root cause because the logs are not correlated. You need to implement a solution that allows you to follow a single user request across all microservices involved in the transaction. The solution must not require developers to manually add correlation logic to their application code. What should you do?

options.A: Require developers to generate a unique correlation - id at the frontend, and manually add it as a field to every log message in all services.
options.B: Configure all containers to write logs to STDOUT/STDERR, and then filter logs by pod name and timestamp in the Logs Explorer.
options.C: Create custom metics in Cloud Monitoring for error counts in each service and correlate incident spikes using a shared dashboard.
options.D: Implement Cloud Trace by ensuring the traceparent header is propagated between microservice calls to link logs to a single trace.
